p: Saying: We ought to listen to whatever we are truly taught from the word of God, even by wicked teachers, but in a way so that we abstain from their evil behaviour.
sit in Moses' seat: Because God appointed the order, the Lord would therefore have his word to be heard even from the mouth of hypocrites and hirelings.

All therefore whatsoever they bid you: Provided always that they deliver the doctrine of Moses which they profess, which thing the metaphor of the seat shows, which they occupied as teachers of Moses' teaching.
For they bind heavy burdens and: For the most part hypocrites most severely exact those things which they themselves chiefly neglect.
But all their works they do: Hypocrites are ambitious.

phylacteries: It was a thread or ribband of blue silk in the fringe of a corner, the beholding of which made them remember the laws and ordinances of God: and therefore it was called a phylactery, or as you would say, a container. See Nu 15:38; De 6:8, a commandment which the Jews abused afterwards, as those do today who hang the gospel of John around their necks, which was condemned many years ago in the Council of Antioch.
the borders of their garments: Literally, "Twisted tassels of thread which hung at the outermost hems of their garments."
synagogues: When assemblies and councils are gathered together.

Rabbi: This word "Rabbi" signifies one that is above his fellows, and is as good as any of them: and we may see by the repeating of it how proud a title it was. Now they were called Rabbi who, by the laying on of hands, were uttered and declared to the world to be wise men.
But be not ye: Modesty is a singular ornament of God's minsters.

called Rabbi: Seek not ambitiously after it: for our Lord does not forbid us to give the magistrate and our masters the honour that is due to them; Augustine in a sermon on the words of God from Mt 11:1-30.
one is your Master: He seems to allude to references in Isa 54:13 and Jer 31:34.
father upon the earth: He attacks a custom of the Jews, for they called the rabbis "our fathers".
masters: It seems that the scribes hunted very greatly after such titles, these scribes being the ones whom he called blind guides in Mt 23:16.
shall exalt himself shall be abased: He seems to allude to the position of the rabbis, for rabbi signifies one that is in a high position.
But woe unto you: Hypocrites cannot endure others to be better than themselves.
hypocrites: Christ, when he reproves any man sharply, uses this word to show us that there is nothing more detestable than hypocrisy and falsehood in religion.
entering to go in: Who are even at the door.
Woe unto you: It is a common thing among hypocrites to abuse the pretence of zeal when in reality they are exercising covetousness and extortion.

for a pretence make long prayer: Literally, "under a colour of long praying"; and the word "and" signifies a double wickedness in them: the one, that they devoured widows goods: the other that they did it under a pretence of godliness.
land to make one proselyte: The dry part: now that part of the earth is called dry which the Lord has given to us to live upon.
is a debtor: Is a debtor. In the Syrian language, sins are called "Debts", and it is certain that Christ spoke in Syrian.
sanctifieth the gold: Causes the gold which is dedicated to a holy use to be considered holy.
throne of God: If heaven is God's throne, than he is without doubt above this entire world.
Woe unto you: Hypocrites take special care in small matters, and neglect the things which matter the very most.
faith: Faithfulness in the keeping of promises.
Woe unto you: Hypocrites pay too much attention to outward things, and the inward things they utterly condemn.
Woe unto you: Hypocrites, when they try the most to cover up their wickedness, it is then by the just judgment of God that they shame themselves.
Fill ye up then the measure: A proverb used by the Jews, which has this meaning: You go on also, and follow your ancestors, that at length your wickedness may come to its fulness.
Wherefore: Hypocrites are cruel.
That upon you may come all: The punishment of those who persecute the gospel, under the pretence of zeal.
Barachias: Of Joiada, who was also called Barach-jah, that is, blessed of the Lord.
O Jerusalem: Where the mercy of God was greatest, it was there that there was the greatest wickedness and rebellion, and at length the sharpest judgments of God.

gathered thy children together: He speaks of the outward ministry, and as he was promised for the saving of this people, he was making sure that it would happen, even from the time that the promise was made to Abraham.
